entry.name: mcs.wave~
entry.description: wave~ reads from a portion of a buffer~ to produce a repeating waveform, given a signal input that goes between 0 and 1 (for example, using a phasor~) to define the position in the buffer. When the wave~ object is instantiated as mcs.wave~ its outputs are combined into a single multichannel output but otherwise it functions identically to wave~.

arguments.name: buffer-name
arguments.description: Obligatory. Names theobject whose sample memory is used byfor its stored waveform. Note that if the underlying data in achanges, the signal output ofwill change, since it does not copy the sample data in a.always uses the first channel of a multi-channel.

arguments.name: start-point
arguments.description: After thename argument, you can type in a value for the start and end points of the waveform as millisecond offset from the beginning of aobject's sample memory. By default, the start point is 0. If you want to set a non-zero start point but retain the sample end as the waveform end point, use only a single typed-in argument after thename. Theobject uses thesampling rate to determine loop points. If ais connected to the start point (middle) inlet, the initial waveform start point argument is ignored.

arguments.name: end-point
arguments.description: After the start point argument, you can type in a value for the end point of the waveform, as a millisecond offsets from the beginning of aobject's sample memory. By default, the end point is the end of the sample. If ais connected to the end point (right) inlet, the initial waveform end point is ignored.

arguments.name: number-of-output-channels
arguments.description: Sets the number of output channels, which determines the number of outlets that theobject will have. If theobject being played byhas more channels than the number of outputs of, the extra channels are not played. If theobject has fewer channels, the extrasignal outputs are 0.

attributes.name: interp
attributes.digest: Set the wavetable interpolation mode
attributes.description: The interpolation modes are:-- No interpolation. Wavetable interpolation is disabled using the interp 0 message.- High-quality linear interpolation (default)- Low-quality linear interpolation. This mode uses the interpolation method found in MSP 1.x versions of theobject. While this mode is faster than mode 1, it cannot playobjects of arbitrary length and produces more interpolation artifacts.- Cosine interpolation- Cubic interpolation- Spline interpolation- Hermite interpolation

messages.digest: Open a file buffer display window
messages.description: Double-clicking on theobject will open a window that displays the audio file loaded in the buffer associated with the object.

messages.name: float
messages.description: In middle or right inlets: Numbers can be used instead of signal objects to control the start and end points of the waveform, provided ais not connected to the inlet that receives the number. Theobject uses thesampling rate to determine loop points.

messages.name: int
messages.description: In middle or right inlets: Numbers can be used instead of signal objects to control the start and end points of the waveform, provided ais not connected to the inlet that receives the number. Theobject uses thesampling rate to determine loop points.

messages.name: list
messages.description: A list message sent to the left inlet with two values will set the start and end points of the waveform in milliseconds. The first value determines the start point and the second value determines the endpoint.

messages.name: set
messages.digest: Set theused byfor its stored waveform
messages.description: The word, followed by a, sets theused byfor its stored waveform. Thecan optionally be followed by two values setting new waveform start and end points. If the values are not present, the default start and end points (the start and end of the sample) are used. If signal objects are connected to the start and/or end point inlets, the start and/or end point values are ignored.

messages.name: signal
messages.description: In left inlet: Input signal values progressing from 0 to 1 are used to scan a specified range of samples in aobject. The output of acan be used to controlas an oscillator, treating the range of samples in theas a repeating waveform. However, note that when changing the frequency of aconnected to the left inlet of, the perceived pitch of the signal coming out ofmay not correspond exactly to the frequency ofitself if the stored waveform contains multiple or partial repetitions of a waveform. You can invert theto play the waveform backwards.In middle inlet: The start of the waveform as a millisecond offset from the beginning of aobject's sample memory.In right inlet: The end of the waveform as a millisecond offset from the beginning of aobject's sample memory.
